title: (Dis)consent: A Night of Performance and Installations
description: A night of performance and interactive installations questioning how consent is negotiated across bodies, algorithms, and ecological systems.

images.alt: Yellow graphic artwork over a floral photograph

introduction: Presented by MESH_ARTS and UAAD, (Dis)consent brought performances, interactive installations, and live generative media into dialogue. Visitors could command bodies, contribute data, alter generated images, and participate in speculative ecological systems. The program asked whether refusal, withdrawal, and renegotiation remain possible once we are already embedded in a system.

title: Worlds Adrift: UAAD x Creative Code Art
description: An evening of live A/V performances and video works tracing frequencies, ruptures, and worlds in transit.
introduction: Co-organized by Creative Code Art and UAAD, Worlds Adrift assembled artists from around the world for a temporary environment of video, sound, and live A/V performance. The works moved between geographies, languages, and natural and artificial systems, allowing images and sounds to overlap before dispersing.

title: Attention // Distraction
description: A two-day UAAD program exploring how attention is shaped and contested by digital culture, with approximately 250 visitors.
introduction: Presented by UAAD at The Blanc, Attention // Distraction examined the forces that direct our attention and the things left outside the frame. Interactive installations, net art, XR, artist-made games, algorithmic systems, live performance, and talks treated distraction as a tool for refusal, interference, and subversion.

title: Neuromantics
description: A playable Soho exhibition of artist-made games, XR, live interfaces, and moving-image works.
introduction: Co-curated with Danielle Paterson, Neuromantics turned a Soho loft into a playable ecosystem. Artists created worlds with their own rules, some open and others unlocked through collaboration, exchange, or participation. Visitors shaped what each work revealed, while evening live sets activated the space through audio interfaces and experimental sound.

title: nodes: i x Processing Foundation x ARTIFICE
description: An evening of talk, installation, and live coding performances connecting nodes:i, Processing, Artifice, and UAAD.
introduction: An evening at NYU Tandon at The Yard exploring creative tools, resource networks, and cultural infrastructure. Presented with Artifice, Processing Foundation, and UAAD, the program brought a talk by Moon Davé together with installation and live coded performances.

title: TechnoMirage: AI x Speculative Futures
description: An in-person gathering at Index NYC exploring AI and speculative futures through conversation, a workshop, installations, and performance.
introduction: Co-organized by UAAD and Liminal at Index NYC, TechnoMirage asked what stories AI erases and how artists might reclaim them. The gathering brought panel discussion, a workshop, installations, and performance into a shared inquiry about speculative futures and creative agency.

title: Reconfiguring Creativity: AI, Ethics and Emerging Practices
description: A public panel on AI, ethics, and creative practice presented with Parsons School of Design.
introduction: Presented by Parsons School of Design and UAAD as part of the Design with AI course, this panel brought artists, designers, educators, and researchers into dialogue about how AI reshapes artistic practice and the ethical questions that follow.

title: [EX UTERO]: ARTIFICE 004 BLACKBOX
description: A sequential new media performance at ARTIFICE 004 that staged collapse as a site of new beginnings.
introduction: The apocalypse has arrived. Final cries are swallowed in liquid ruin. Time fractures, collapses, and disappears. No origin, no inherited form. Life no longer emerges from the womb but through rupture, mutation, and synthetic gestation. [Ex Utero], Latin for "outside the womb" or "beyond the uterus," is rebirth without a blueprint—an existence forged in the breakdown of structures, where form is never fixed, only recombined. [Ex Utero] showcases six artifacts from the digital realm, each a relic of speculative realities, a fragment of mythologies still in flux, and an echo of futures that refuse to solidify. Without a singular lineage, they emerge from a landscape of continuing transformation, where species, bodies, and languages dissolve into one another. No Garden of Eden. No return to dust. The mutants only remain in the ceaseless becoming.

title: Jukebox of Dissonance: The UAAD Festival
description: A two-day UAAD festival of live performance, virtual curation, artist talks, film, and workshops.
introduction: Organized for UAAD’s second anniversary, Jukebox of Dissonance brought a virtual exhibition together with two days of live performances, artist talks, discussions, film, and a workshop in New York. Its varied formats invited artists and audiences to meet across disciplines and imagine new connections between art, technology, and collective practice.

title: Ghosts in the Feedback Loop
description: An immersive virtual exhibition exploring how people erased or distorted by algorithms can reclaim technological space.
introduction: In the feedback loops of machine learning, certain bodies, cultures, and ways of knowing are made visible, distorted, or erased. Like ghosts—excluded yet ever-present—they haunt the machine. They slip through algorithmic blind spots, bend systems’ logic, and disrupt with glitches and ruptures that unsettle computational control. But ghosts don’t just haunt—they rewire. They assert presence, reframe meaning, and speak in forms the system was never trained to understand. Through cracks in the loop, they reemerge as designers of new imaginaries for themselves and for the communities the system failed to see.

Matrix of the Not-Yet
description: An interactive web-based curatorial project mapping possible worlds across social, technological, and ecological intersections.
introduction: An interactive publication featuring 19 artist groups. Inspired by the rhizome, Matrix of the Not-Yet replaces a linear reading path with a decentralized network of visions for possible futures.

title: Alt-Alterity: An Immersive Virtual Exhibition
description: A virtual exhibition featuring 26 artist groups from 13 countries, exploring alternative forms of identity and relation.
introduction: In the midst of gathering storms — genocides, wars, forced displacements, global climate collapse, the ascendency of technocracy, alongside the unyielding presence of unjust ideologies such as sexism, racism, colonialism, imperialism, and capitalism — emerges our curatorial and editorial initiative, Alt-Alterity. It stands as an attempt to provoke a co-imagination of an alternative paradigm for how we, as humans, engage with both the “other” inhabitants of our planet and “each other” within our societies.

title: Ties That Cannot Be Unbound
description: A virtual exhibition reconsidering our relationships with living and non-living entities.
introduction: Our lives are shaped by the ties that bind us to the world around us. These ties weave networks of relationships that make up our narratives and help us navigate the complexities of our planet. UAAD invites you to explore these connections with Ties That Cannot Be Unbound, an online exhibition that discusses the interconnectedness of spirituality and physicality, the blurred boundaries between the living and the non-living, and the ties between our bodies and the environment. Featuring outstanding works in sound, image, film, and interaction, this exhibition responds to the question: what kinds of ties are impossible to unbind? Join us on a journey of self-discovery and collective action towards a more sustainable and harmonious future.
